title: EKSU ACC 328 - Elements of Government | Practice Bank

questions.stem: In a confederal system, what is the primary source of authority for the central decision-making body?

options.A: Direct popular mandate from all citizens
options.B: Delegation of powers by sovereign member states
options.C: An independent electoral commission
options.D: A constitution established by a national assembly

questions.stem: The concept of "parliamentary sovereignty" implies that the legislature is the supreme legal authority and can create or end any law. Which of the following is a direct consequence of this principle?

options.A: The judiciary possesses the power of judicial review over all legislation.
options.B: The executive branch is directly elected by the populace.
options.C: No parliament can bind its successor.
options.D: The head of state is also the head of government.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the fundamental difference between a unitary and a federal system of government regarding power distribution?

options.A: Unitary systems concentrate power at the national level, while federal systems divide it between national and sub-national levels.
options.B: Unitary systems rely on a unicameral legislature, while federal systems mandate a bicameral legislature.
options.C: Unitary systems allow for direct citizen participation, while federal systems use representative democracy.
options.D: Unitary systems have a written constitution, while federal systems operate under unwritten conventions.

questions.stem: The introduction of the "Warrant Chief" system in colonial Nigeria primarily aimed to:

options.A: Establish a uniform judicial system across all regions.
options.B: Facilitate indirect rule by co-opting local leaders into the colonial administration.
options.C: Promote democratic participation among indigenous populations.
options.D: Develop modern infrastructure through local taxation.

questions.stem: The principle of "checks and balances" in a presidential system is most directly exemplified by which of the following scenarios?

options.A: The Prime Minister dissolving parliament and calling for new elections.
options.B: The President vetoing a bill passed by the legislature.
options.C: The judiciary issuing an advisory opinion on a proposed law.
options.D: The legislature impeaching a minister for misconduct.

questions.stem: In pre-colonial Igbo society, the role of age-grades in community policing suggests a system that relied heavily on:

options.A: Centralized authority and formal law enforcement.
options.B: Collective responsibility and social pressure.
options.C: A professional, paid police force.
options.D: External intervention from neighboring kingdoms.

questions.stem: The inclusion of "concurrent list" items in a federal constitution signifies:

options.A: Areas exclusively reserved for the federal government.
options.B: Powers that can be exercised by both federal and state governments.
options.C: Matters solely within the purview of state governments.
options.D: Provisions for secession of member states.

questions.stem: The United Nations Security Council's permanent membership with veto power is a mechanism designed to:

options.A: Ensure equitable representation of all member states.
options.B: Prevent the organization from taking action on issues deemed vital to the national interests of major powers.
options.C: Promote the development of international law.
options.D: Facilitate the peaceful resolution of all global disputes.

questions.stem: The "standing committee" in a legislative body is typically characterized by:

options.A: Ad hoc assignments and temporary mandates.
options.B: Members who physically stand during debates.
options.C: Permanent, statutory responsibilities that span legislative sessions.
options.D: A direct reporting line to the head of state.

questions.stem: Government-owned companies operating in sectors like energy, transportation, or telecommunications are best categorized as:

options.A: Public services, focusing solely on essential provision.
options.B: Public enterprises, engaging in commercial activities.
options.C: Public investments, primarily for financial returns.
options.D: Public utilities, exclusively serving the public good.

questions.stem: The formation of the Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP) by Herbert Macaulay in 1923 marked an early attempt to:

options.A: Advocate for complete independence from British rule.
options.B: Mobilize political support within the limited franchise of the time.
options.C: Establish a pan-African nationalist movement.
options.D: Promote economic development through industrialization.

questions.stem: A Commonwealth member that retains the British Monarch as its Head of State, while being a sovereign nation, operates under a system that is most accurately described as:

options.A: A republic with a ceremonial presidency.
options.B: A constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary government.
options.C: A federal system with a directly elected executive.
options.D: An absolute monarchy with delegated powers.

questions.stem: The concept of "judicial review" allows courts to:

options.A: Appoint members of the executive branch.
options.B: Declare legislative acts or executive actions unconstitutional.
options.C: Initiate impeachment proceedings against public officials.
options.D: Grant pardons to convicted individuals.

questions.stem: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 in Nigeria is notable for:

options.A: Introducing universal adult suffrage.
options.B: Establishing a federal system with a strong central government.
options.C: Creating a bicameral legislature at the federal level.
options.D: Expanding regional autonomy and representation.

questions.stem: The primary purpose of the "first reading" of a bill in a legislature is to:

options.A: Debate the merits and demerits of the proposed legislation.
options.B: Formally introduce the bill to the legislative body and allow for its distribution.
options.C: Conduct public hearings to gather stakeholder input.
options.D: Vote on whether to approve or reject the bill.

questions.stem: Nigeria's involvement in UN peacekeeping operations, such as in the Congo, demonstrates its commitment to:

options.A: Asserting regional dominance.
options.B: Upholding international peace and security.
options.C: Promoting its own economic interests abroad.
options.D: Establishing military alliances.

questions.stem: The "family" is considered a primary agent of political socialization because it:

options.A: Directly disseminates government propaganda.
options.B: Shapes an individual's initial values, beliefs, and attitudes towards politics.
options.C: Organizes formal political education programs.
options.D: Controls the flow of information through mass media.

questions.stem: The behavioral approach in political science emphasizes:

options.A: The study of formal institutions and structures of government.
options.B: The systematic, empirical observation and analysis of political phenomena, often using quantitative methods.
options.C: The philosophical underpinnings of political thought.
options.D: The historical evolution of political systems.

questions.stem: The principle of "federal character" in Nigeria's constitution aims to:

options.A: Ensure the dominance of one ethnic group in national affairs.
options.B: Promote national unity and equitable representation across different regions and ethnic groups.
options.C: Establish a purely merit-based system for public appointments.
options.D: Grant special privileges to minority ethnic groups.

questions.stem: A significant problem of Nigeria's federalism has been the imbalance in the structure of the federation, often manifesting as:

options.A: Overly strong and autonomous regional governments.
options.B: An excessive concentration of power and resources at the federal level.
options.C: A lack of competition between federating units.
options.D: The absence of a clear division of powers.

questions.stem: The executive power of withholding assent to a bill passed by the legislature is a manifestation of the principle of:

options.A: Collective responsibility among ministers.
options.B: Separation of powers and checks and balances.
options.C: Parliamentary supremacy.
options.D: Judicial independence.

questions.stem: In the British parliamentary system, the monarch's role as "Queen-in-Parliament" signifies:

options.A: The monarch's direct legislative power.
options.B: The monarch's symbolic and constitutional role within the legislative process.
options.C: The monarch's absolute control over parliamentary proceedings.
options.D: The monarch's power to dissolve Parliament unilaterally.

questions.stem: Totalitarianism is fundamentally characterized by:

options.A: The existence of multiple, competing political parties.
options.B: A single, all-encompassing ideology and a single recognized political party that controls all aspects of public and private life.
options.C: Decentralized power with significant autonomy for regional governments.
options.D: A strong emphasis on individual liberties and freedoms.

questions.stem: Max Weber's ideal bureaucracy includes "hierarchy" as a critical element, which refers to:

options.A: A system of checks and balances between different departments.
options.B: A clear chain of command with defined levels of authority.
options.C: The absence of formal rules and procedures.
options.D: The direct election of all administrative officials.

questions.stem: According to Marxist theory, the "bourgeoisie" are those who:

options.A: Own the means of production and distribution.
options.B: Sell their labor power for wages.
options.C: Are landless peasants.
options.D: Control religious institutions.

questions.stem: Which of the following books is *not* primarily authored by Karl Marx?

options.A: The Communist Manifesto
options.B: Das Kapital
options.C: Wealth of the Nations
options.D: The Critique of Political Economy

questions.stem: A political ideology that advocates for static ownership and control of the means of production, often characterized by a rigid social structure and a strong, centralized authority, is most closely aligned with:

options.A: Socialism
options.B: Fascism
options.C: Communalism
options.D: Feudalism

questions.stem: In a capitalist system, the "proletariat" refers to:

options.A: The owners of capital and means of production.
options.B: The working class who sell their labor.
options.C: The landed aristocracy.
options.D: The merchant class.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT typically considered a political ideology?

options.A: Fascism
options.B: Capitalism
options.C: Nazism
options.D: Atheism

questions.stem: Fascism, as a political ideology, gained prominence and was propagated primarily in:

options.A: Germany
options.B: Italy
options.C: Russia
options.D: Spain

questions.stem: Factors that enhance Nigeria's foreign relations typically include:

options.A: Economic dependence on external powers.
options.B: Non-interference in the affairs of other states.
options.C: A policy of isolationism.
options.D: Aggressive territorial expansion.

questions.stem: A key characteristic of authoritarianism is that government is often:

options.A: Decentralized and consultative.
options.B: Personalized, with power concentrated in the hands of a single leader or a small group, and limited accountability.
options.C: Based on broad consensus and public participation.
options.D: Strictly limited by a constitution with strong judicial oversight.

questions.stem: The Emirate system in the administration of Hausa/Fulani society was fundamentally:

options.A: Democratic and participatory.
options.B: Hierarchical, with power flowing from the Emir downwards.
options.C: Secular and egalitarian.
options.D: Based on direct elections by the populace.

questions.stem: The International Court of Justice (ICJ), the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, is located in:

options.A: Geneva
options.B: The Hague
options.C: New York
options.D: Paris

questions.stem: The first Premier of the Western Region of Nigeria was:

options.A: Ladoke Akintola
options.B: Obafemi Awolowo
options.C: Nnamdi Azikiwe
options.D: Ahmadu Bello

questions.stem: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 in Nigeria is significant for:

options.A: Establishing a unitary system of government.
options.B: Granting full independence to Nigeria.
options.C: Introducing a federal structure with greater regional autonomy.
options.D: Abolishing the office of the Governor.

questions.stem: The ability of courts to declare legislative acts or executive actions unconstitutional is known as:

options.A: Habeas Corpus
options.B: Judicial Review
options.C: Certiorari
options.D: Mandamus

questions.stem: The first military coup d'état in Nigeria led to the death of which Head of State?

options.A: General Yakubu Gowon
options.B: General Murtala Mohammed
options.C: General Aguiyi Ironsi
options.D: General Olusegun Obasanjo

questions.stem: Centralization of power is a defining feature of:

options.A: Confederal government
options.B: Unitary government
options.C: Federal government
options.D: Presidential government

questions.stem: Which of the following is generally NOT considered a major source of local government revenue in Nigeria?

options.A: Property taxes
options.B: Statutory allocations from federal and state governments
options.C: Direct foreign investment
options.D: Market fees and licenses

questions.stem: The function of "recruitment of leaders" in a modern state is primarily performed by:

options.A: The judiciary
options.B: The executive branch
options.C: Elections
options.D: The civil service

questions.stem: The structure of the civil service is typically based on:

options.A: Patronage organization
options.B: Hierarchical organization
options.C: Horizontal organization
options.D: Direct democracy

questions.stem: Before the establishment of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU), Africa had blocs such as:

options.A: Monrovia, Accra, and Casablanca
options.B: Brazzaville, Zimbabwe, and Monrovia
options.C: Casablanca, Brazzaville, and Monrovia
options.D: Algiers, Monrovia, and Casablanca

questions.stem: Oligarchy is a form of government that:

options.A: Protects the interests of the common people through direct participation.
options.B: Disregards the views and rights of the minority.
options.C: Enhances the interests of a small, ruling elite.
options.D: Promotes widespread social and economic equality.

questions.stem: A critical element for maintaining confidence in the electoral process includes:

options.A: The observation of limited franchise.
options.B: Periodic free and fair elections.
options.C: The appointment of partisan electoral officers.
options.D: The absence of law enforcement agencies at polling stations.

questions.stem: In a parliamentary system, the executive derives its legitimacy from:

options.A: A direct popular vote, independent of the legislature.
options.B: The confidence and support of the legislature.
options.C: The appointment by the head of state.
options.D: A constitutional referendum.

questions.stem: The concept of "separation of powers" in government aims to:

options.A: Consolidate all governmental authority in one branch.
options.B: Prevent the concentration of power by dividing governmental functions among distinct branches.
options.C: Ensure the dominance of the legislative over the executive.
options.D: Facilitate swift decision-making without checks.

questions.stem: The "rule of law" principle dictates that:

options.A: Government officials are above the law.
options.B: All individuals, including those in power, are subject to and accountable under the law.
options.C: Laws can be arbitrarily changed by the ruling party.
options.D: Judicial decisions are not binding on the executive.

questions.stem: An electoral system that uses proportional representation aims to:

options.A: Ensure that the party with the most votes wins all seats in a district.
options.B: Allocate seats in the legislature in proportion to the votes received by each party.
options.C: Favor smaller parties by giving them disproportionate representation.
options.D: Elect candidates based solely on their personal popularity.

questions.stem: The primary function of an electoral system is to:

options.A: Determine the ideology of the ruling party.
options.B: Provide a mechanism for the peaceful transfer of power and representation of the electorate.
options.C: Control the flow of information to the public.
options.D: Enforce laws and maintain public order.

questions.stem: In the context of Nigerian federalism, the "exclusive list" refers to matters:

options.A: On which both federal and state governments can legislate.
options.B: Solely within the legislative competence of the federal government.
options.C: Reserved for the exclusive jurisdiction of state governments.
options.D: That are not subject to any form of government regulation.

questions.stem: The "vote of no confidence" is a mechanism primarily found in:

options.A: Presidential systems, to remove the President.
options.B: Parliamentary systems, to remove the government or a minister.
options.C: Federal systems, to dissolve state legislatures.
options.D: Unitary systems, to challenge local government officials.

questions.stem: The concept of "impeachment" is a process used to:

options.A: Elect new members of parliament.
options.B: Remove a high-ranking public official from office due to misconduct.
options.C: Grant amnesty to political prisoners.
options.D: Appoint judges to the supreme court.

questions.stem: The "Head of State" in a parliamentary system is typically distinct from the "Head of Government" in that:

options.A: The Head of State is the chief executive, while the Head of Government is ceremonial.
options.B: The Head of State is a monarch or president with largely ceremonial duties, while the Head of Government (Prime Minister) leads the executive.
options.C: Both roles are always held by the same individual.
options.D: The Head of State is elected, while the Head of Government is appointed.

questions.stem: The establishment of the office of the Warrant Chief in Eastern Nigeria during the colonial era was an attempt to:

options.A: Implement direct British rule without local intermediaries.
options.B: Create a more democratic and representative local governance structure.
options.C: Formalize and utilize existing traditional leadership structures for administrative purposes.
options.D: Introduce a Western-style judicial system.

questions.stem: The principle of "collective responsibility" in a parliamentary system means that:

options.A: Individual ministers are solely accountable for their portfolios.
options.B: The entire cabinet is responsible for government policies, and ministers must publicly support them or resign.
options.C: The opposition party is equally responsible for government actions.
options.D: The Head of State bears ultimate responsibility for all government decisions.

questions.stem: The "Lyttleton Constitution" of 1954 in Nigeria is significant for:

options.A: Introducing universal adult suffrage nationwide.
options.B: Establishing a federal system with three regions and a federal legislature.
options.C: Granting Nigeria full independence.
options.D: Abolishing the office of the Governor-General.

questions.stem: The concept of "political socialization" refers to the process by which:

options.A: Political leaders are elected to office.
options.B: Individuals acquire political attitudes, values, and beliefs.
options.C: Laws are enacted and enforced.
options.D: International relations are conducted.

questions.stem: The "behavioural revolution" in political science advocated for:

options.A: A return to classical political philosophy.
options.B: The application of scientific methods, including empirical observation and quantitative analysis, to the study of political phenomena.
options.C: A focus on the historical development of political institutions.
options.D: The study of political ideologies in isolation from practice.

questions.stem: The principle of "separation of powers" is most strongly associated with which form of government?

options.A: Parliamentary system
options.B: Presidential system
options.C: Confederal system
options.D: Unitary system
